A serum albumin level of 2.1 to 2.7 g/dL is an indication of a moderate degree of visceral protein 
depletion caused by decreased protein absorption. Muscle wasting and weakness are signs of skel­
etal protein depletion.

This calcium value of 6.7 mg/dL, corrected for JR’s albumin level, still is not in the normal range 
of 8.7 to 10.2 mg/dL. The recommended calcium intake for 19 to 30 years of age is 1000 mg/day. 
Most calcium absorption occurs in the duodenum, but all small intestinal segments absorb calcium. 
When adjustments are made for transit time and the relative lengths of the different intestinal seg­
ments, both the jejunum and ileum contribute substantially to overall calcium absorption. JR’s
